context: A police archivist guides a uni reporter through old records
purpose: Teach: 暦/酸化/復元/錯覚/混合/死後/政令/悪影響

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: この棚が戦前の記録でね、旧暦で日付が書かれているものも多いんだ。
lines.en: These shelves hold prewar records, and many of them are dated using the old lunar calendar.
lines.style: Calm archivist tone, measured pace, slight pride in showing the materials.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 紙が随分変色していますね。やはり酸化が進んでいるんですか？
lines.en: The paper has discolored quite a bit. Is oxidation really progressing that much?
lines.style: Curious young reporter, polite keigo, leaning in to examine the documents.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: ああ、湿気と光で悪影響が出るんだ。最近やっと一部をデータで復元できるようになってね。
lines.en: Yes, humidity and light cause damage. Recently we've finally been able to digitally restore some of it.
lines.style: Patient explanation, weathered voice of someone who's done this for decades.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 復元というと、文字が消えたところを推定するんでしょうか。
lines.en: When you say restore, do you mean estimating where the characters have faded away?
lines.style: Sharp follow-up question, journalist's instinct kicking in mid-sentence.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 推定もあるが、画像を混合して輪郭を浮かび上がらせる。一見読めるように見えるが、錯覚の場合もある。
lines.en: Some estimation, but we blend images to reveal the outlines. It may look readable, but sometimes it's an illusion.
lines.style: Cautious veteran, lowering voice slightly to stress the warning.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。ところで、戦後の政令で公開できなくなった資料もあると聞きました。
lines.en: I see. By the way, I heard some materials became unreleasable due to postwar cabinet ordinances.
lines.style: Probing gently, testing how far the archivist will open up.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: よく調べてるな。当事者の死後五十年経たないと出せない書類もあるよ。
lines.en: You've done your homework. Some documents can't be released until fifty years after the person's death.
lines.style: Mildly impressed chuckle, then back to professional reserve.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: それでも記録が残っているだけありがたいです。ぜひ記事で紹介させてください。
lines.en: Even so, I'm grateful the records remain at all. Please let me feature them in my article.
lines.style: Earnest closing, slight bow in voice, eager but respectful.
